start.text: The morning smells of cut grass and new uniforms. {player_name} checks his coat pocket for the third time: the note is still there, folded in four, the ink so smudged that only one sentence can be read.

start__2.text: "Come back. School is boring without you."

intro2.text: There's no signature. He doesn't remember who wrote it, or why he kept it. He only knows that, the first time he read it, his chest tightened as if he had forgotten to tell someone he was leaving.

hallway.text: The main hallway is full of the usual first-day noise: laughter, hurried steps, someone shouting a name from across the courtyard. Nothing out of the ordinary. Yet.

loop_echo.text: At the entrance, he feels he has walked through this gate before. The steps are worn exactly to the shape of his stride. The woman at the office will say "welcome back" in two minutes, and he already knows with which smile.

core.text: First day. {player_name} walks through the school gate carrying more hope than he'd care to admit — a fresh start, maybe. A chance to be another version of himself, even if just a little.

outro1.text: At the office, a woman hands him his class schedule and a locker key.

outro1__2.text: She smiles with the warmth of someone who has said this many times: "Welcome back." He politely corrects her: it's his first time here.

outro2.text: At the end of the hallway, the four doors of the literature club are open. From inside comes the sound of laughter and paper being folded. {player_name} follows the noise without deciding to, like someone following a thread.

start.text: The night was short. He dreamed of a room with no windows and a clock that only had an hour hand.

start__2.text: He woke before the alarm, feeling he'd forgotten to do something important at nine the night before.

intro2.text: On the way to school, the traffic light at the corner turns red three times in a row, with no cars passing. {player_name} waits through all three, because something in him thinks waiting matters.

aftermath.text: The normal voice returns. It finishes the announcement about the class schedule.

aftermath__2.text: No one looked up. No one heard. {player_name} looks around and counts: thirty students, thirty calm faces. He is the only one who stopped breathing.

loop_echo.text: The announcement will glitch at 8:02. He knows. He watches the clock, waiting, and feels no fear. Only tiredness.

core.text: Second day. The school's sound system plays the usual announcement before first period — and then, for half a second, the voice changes.

outro1.text: At break, he asks a classmate if he heard the strange voice in the morning announcement. The classmate gives back a vague smile: "What strange voice?" The answer comes too fast, like a memorized line.

outro2.text: At the end of the day, {player_name} stares at the rusty speaker in the hallway. No voice comes out of it. But its cable is unplugged from the wall, and that makes no sense at all.

start.text: The rain started before dawn and didn't stop.

start__2.text: The bus windows fog up and the driver changes stations whenever the music gets good. {player_name} traces the initials K.M. on the glass with his finger without noticing, and wipes them off with his sleeve when he does.

intro2.text: At the entrance, the puddle before the gate reflects a building taller than the school. He steps into it on purpose, and the reflection vanishes.

desk.text: In the row by the window there's an empty desk. No one sits there. Someone carved two letters into the wood: K.M.
choices: Let it go and pay attention in class.

ask.speaker: Teacher
ask.text: That one? It's been empty since the start of the year. There was a spare desk in the room, that's all.

ignore.text: {player_name} opens his notebook and tries to copy the board. The pen slips. He wrote "K.M." in the margin without noticing.

flash.text:
Cold wind. The smell of rain. A metal railing, wet, under his palm.

Someone laughs.

Then the classroom comes back. Chalk on the board. The headache stays.

loop_echo.text: The desk with the initials K.M. is where it has always been. This time he doesn't even need to look at it. He already knows where every scratch is.

core.text: Third day. The teacher calls the roll out loud, name by name. {player_name} notices she skips a line on the list — her eyes stop there for half a second and move on.

outro1.text: At the end of the day, the teacher takes him aside and asks, quietly, if he's sleeping well.

outro1__2.text: It feels like she wants to ask something else, as if the real question were hidden inside another one, like nesting dolls.

outro2.text: {player_name} says yes. She nods slowly and looks one last time at the empty desk. "If you ever need someone to talk to," she says, and stops. "Someone always does."

start.text: He woke up early, without an alarm. The house is too quiet, like a classroom after a lesson that ended too soon.

start__2.text: On the kitchen table there's a plate of cold toast and a note from his mother: "Back late."

intro2.text: He shoves his coat into his backpack without really looking. Had he looked, he'd have seen it was still damp, as if it had spent the night in the rain.

open.text: The handwriting is his. Not similar to his — it is his, with the same crooked way of writing the letter "a". The entries have dates. Day 5. Day 6.

open__2.text: Day 7. Days that haven't happened yet.
choices: Close the notebook and throw it away.

read.speaker: Notebook
read.text: "Day 6: woke up with my hands hurt again. Day 8: the roof door was open. Day 11: don't trust the beautiful day. Day 12: don't let him go up alone."

trash.text: He throws the notebook into the hallway trash and goes to class. At break, when he opens his backpack, the notebook is inside. He didn't put it there.

torn.text:
The pages after Day 12 have been torn out.

On the last one left, a name, written over and over. Fainter each time. As if the pen were running out.

Or the memory.

loop_echo.text: The notebook will be in the locker. He leaves it there, unopened. But tomorrow, and the day after, and the day after that, he'll open it. He always does.

core.text: Fourth day. Before first period, {player_name} opens his hallway locker to put away his coat. There's a notebook inside. Black cover, no name.

outro1.text: In the afternoon, at the library, the librarian hands him a list of old loans he never asked for.

outro1__2.text: His name appears on every line, with dates he doesn't remember living through, always the same book: a volume of short stories with no author.

outro2.text: He doesn't open the book. But as he returns the list, he notices the librarian's eyes are wet and she doesn't know why. "Sorry," she says, laughing awkwardly. "Someday I'll remember."

start.text: The courtyard woke up full of colored ribbons, almost on purpose. Someone spent the night hanging decorations in the trees without anyone seeing.

start__2.text: Students arrive in groups, laughing and checking their phones, while the wind sways the ribbons.

intro2.text: {player_name} feels his right hand tingle, as if he'd slept on it. He opens and closes his fingers. The scar on his palm, a thin pale line, looks deeper than yesterday.

festival.text: Everyone cheers. {player_name} feels his stomach drop. Day 12. The last date in the notebook.

announcement.speaker: Loudspeaker
announcement.text: Notice from the office: student Kaito Mori, class 2-B, please come in to hand over the documents for—

correction.speaker: Loudspeaker
correction.text: ...Sorry. System error. There is no student by that name.

laugh.text: A few people laugh. Across the courtyard, {player_name} sees Maya, Alice, Hikari and Yuna. None of the four is laughing.

rain.text:
Rain. A roof. A hand slipping out of his.

A voice, laughing:

"I'm still braver than you."

loop_echo.text: The principal is about to announce the festival. He mouths the speech along with him, the same pauses, the same bad jokes.

core.text: Fifth day. Assembly in the courtyard. The principal cheerfully announces that the culture festival will be in a week — on day 12, at night, with lanterns all over the courtyard.

outro1.text: After the assembly, students line up for tissue paper and bamboo sticks. Each class will make its own lanterns.

outro1__2.text: The teacher hands out the sheets in silence and leaves one, with no owner, on the desk at the back.

outro2.text: No one complains about the spare sheet. It's as if everyone knew, somewhere deep down, that it already had an owner. {player_name} folds the white paper carefully and writes no name.

start.text: The bathroom mirror shows a face too tired for his age. {player_name} washes his hands slowly, more for the pain than the dirt. The water in the drain swirls pink for a few seconds.

intro2.text: On his phone, three missed calls from a number with no name, all between 2:12 and 2:15 a.m. He calls back. On the other end, only the sound of rain, and then someone breathing.

memory.text: He doesn't remember the night. He remembers lying down. Then, nothing. His shoe by the bedroom door is wet, and it didn't rain.
choices: Bandage the hand and go to school as if nothing happened.

notebook.speaker: Notebook
notebook.text: "Day 6: woke up with my hands hurt again." Below it, in newer, shakier handwriting that wasn't there yesterday: "You pounded on the door until you bled. It didn't open.

school.text: At school, at the end of the hallway, the stairs to the roof are blocked off with a chain. On the wall beside them, scratched deep into the plaster, as if done with fingernails:

wall.text:
DON'T GO UP.

The handwriting is his. There's plaster dust under the nails of his hurt hand.

loop_echo.text: His hands hurt in the same place, at the same time. He already left a bandage ready in the drawer. Some part of him learned before he did.

core.text: Sixth day. {player_name} wakes to his alarm and a pain that shouldn't be there. The knuckles of his right hand are raw. There's dried blood on his pajama sleeve.

outro1.text: At lunch, Hikari passes him in the hallway with both hands hidden in her jacket pockets. Their eyes meet.

outro1__2.text: She looks away too fast, and he notices that she can't close her fingers properly either.

outro2__2.text: But for the rest of the day they recognize each other without looking: the same way of hiding a palm, the same tiredness of someone who spent the night doing something they can't remember.

start.text: The day starts wrong in small details. The tap water tastes like metal.

start__2.text: The oven clock reads 21:47 even at noon, and his mother, who is never late, doesn't even mention it. {player_name} leaves without breakfast.

intro2.text: On the bus, no one speaks. The driver keeps his eyes on the rearview mirror, not on the road, and takes the turns from memory.

intro2__2.text: When they reach the school, he slows down and murmurs: "Get off here, son. Today it's here."

clock.text:
The wall clock is stopped at 21:47.

The teacher keeps glancing at it during class. She doesn't find it strange that it's night at ten in the morning.

photo.text: On the classroom board, last year's class photo. {player_name} was never at this school last year. Even so, he's in the photo, in the back row.

photo__2.text: Next to him, a boy with a blurred face, as if he moved at the exact moment of the flash.

closer.text:
Up close, the blur isn't a blur.

It's several faces, one over another. Each fainter than the last.

One for each loop. Each time everything started over.

hallway.text: In the hallway, students walk a little too slowly. No one talks about the festival now. No one talks about anything. The school feels like a place being remembered by someone who forgot the details.

loop_echo.text: The teacher will glance at the stopped clock. He's already looking too. Two gazes on the same hand, and neither surprised.

core.text: Seventh day. The desk with the letters K.M. is no longer in the room. Where it stood, the floor is a slightly lighter color, as if it had been there for many years — or none.

outro1.text: Late in the afternoon, Alice intercepts him near the office. Without preamble, she holds out her wristwatch: the second hand trembles, tries to move, and goes back.

outro1__2.text: "Four times," she says. "I measured. Four times a minute it tries. And goes back."

outro2.text: She pockets the watch and looks at the hallway where the desk used to be. "If someone erased a person," she murmurs, "they forgot to erase the traces." Then she leaves without waiting for an answer.

start.text: The hallway smells like something he recognizes from very long ago: dust, rust, rain on concrete.

start__2.text: Each step echoes a second later than it should, as if someone were walking right behind him, in the same rhythm, stopping when he stops.

intro2.text: The school is dark. No emergency lights, no hum of a refrigerator.

intro2__2.text: Only the blue light of a moon that shouldn't be there, since outside, through the window, the sky is cloudy and starless.

chain.text: The chain on the roof stairs lies on the floor, cut. The metal door up above is open. Cold wind comes down the steps. "It never opens before day 8," the notebook said.

cant_leave.text:
He turns and walks toward the exit. The hallway is longer than it should be.

At the end of it, the same stairs. The same open door.

There's no other way tonight.

climb.text: On the other side of the door there's no roof. There's the school. Another school. Broken windows. Stacked desks, rotten.

climb__2.text: Black water covering the courtyard, as if this place had been forgotten for much longer than it has existed.

wall.text:
Tally marks on the wall. Dozens. Hundreds. The oldest almost gone. The newest deep and fresh.

Below, in his handwriting:

"HE DIDN'T JUMP. YOU DIDN'T PUSH. YOU JUST COULDN'T HOLD ON."

maya.text:
You found the place.

...Don't look at me. Look at the wall.

Every mark is a time you came here and chose to go back to the first day.

question.text: I'm going to ask you only once, {player_name}. Do you want to know what really happened? Or do you want me to let you forget? If you choose to forget, I promise I'll make it look like a normal day.

know.text: Then tomorrow I'll tell you everything. Today, just one thing: he was your best friend. And you were the last person he saw.

forget.text: All right. Close your eyes. When you open them, it'll just be stairs, just a locked door, just a normal day.

loop_echo.text: The roof door will be open. He slept in his clothes, so as not to lose time. Maybe that's how he always arrives: ready.

core.text: Eighth day, three in the morning. {player_name} doesn't remember deciding to come. He's in the dark school hallway, in uniform, his bandaged hand throbbing.

outro1.text: The scene dissolves. When he blinks, he's in bed at home, dressed, his shoes dirty with plaster. The alarm reads six in the morning.

outro1__2.text: The sun rises through the window like any other day. But his hand is wrapped in a bandage he doesn't remember putting on.

outro2.text: On the desk, the note from the first day. Someone has added, under the smudged sentence, a line in his handwriting: "You'll come back. You always do."

start.text: There was no dream. For the first time in many days, {player_name} slept without images, without voices, without clocks.

start__2.text: He woke feeling that something had been taken out of him during the night, something heavy, and that the empty space hadn't yet learned to be empty.

intro2.text: His backpack is by the bed, already packed. Inside, the black notebook.

intro2__2.text: The pages after day 12 are still torn out, but now he notices an impression on the paper behind: someone wrote and erased many times, trying to get a single word right.

truth.text: His name was Kaito Mori. You two had been friends since you were little, before you moved away. It was a letter from him that brought you back here. "Come back. School is boring without you."

truth2.text: On the night of the festival, you went up to the roof to watch the fireworks. You argued — something silly, about you taking so long to come back. He climbed onto the railing to tease you. Laughing. "I'm still braver than you."

truth3.text: It was raining. His foot slipped. You grabbed his hand. The railing cut your palm. You held on as long as you could. 21:47. I was on the stairs. I saw your hand become empty.

truth4.text: Since then, every time that night comes, everything goes back to the first day.

truth4__2.text: I don't know if it's you who won't let him go. Or if it's us who won't let you go.

truth4__3.text: I only know that every loop erases a little of him. And then, a little of us.

normal.text: Maya keeps her promise. She greets {player_name} with an ordinary smile and talks about the weather, the festival, the homework. Nothing out of place. A normal, perfect day.

normal2.text: But at lunch, {player_name}'s right hand closes on its own. Hard. As if holding another hand.

normal2__2.text: For a second he feels the rain. The railing cutting his palm.

normal2__3.text: Then the hand opens. And he doesn't remember what he was doing.

outro1f.text:
At night, alone in his room, he repeats the two letters he saw in the notebook: K.M.

It makes no sense. He tries to forget, as he promised Maya, and his hand closes again, on its own, around no one.

loop_echo.text: He already knows what Maya is going to tell him. He hears it again, like rereading a book. The difference is that this time he notices the pause before "I was on the stairs".

core.text: Ninth day. The sun rises in the wrong color, a little gray, like an old photo. Three days left until the festival.
choices: Meet Maya in the hallway, as she promised.
Go to class like on a normal day.

outro1.text: At night, alone in his room, he says the name under his breath, testing its weight. Kaito. It doesn't echo. It doesn't shake the house.

outro1__2.text: It's just a name, an ordinary one, like a neighbor's. But his throat tightens all the same.

outro2.text: Through the window, far away, the school building has one light on, on the top floor. No one should be there. {player_name} watches until the light goes out, and keeps watching after.

start.text: The cafeteria is open, but no one is serving. The stacked trays are still warm. A soup spoon sways by itself in a pot, as if someone had just let go of it.

intro2.text: {player_name} crosses the empty lunchroom listening to his own heart. From somewhere comes the sound of a badly tuned radio, playing an old song he knows the words to and can't place.

window.text: Through the window, at noon, the sun is setting. Stuck in the sky, like wallpaper.

understand.text: {player_name} understands all at once. If everything resets again, the next loop won't have Alice taking notes. Or Hikari running. Or Yuna laughing.

understand__2.text: There'll only be a hallway. A door. And him, alone, not knowing why.

decision.text:
Two days left.

The clock reads 21:47.
choices: "This time I'll hold on to him. Whatever it takes."
"I don't know who he is. But I won't let go."
"I need to stop holding on to this, whatever it is."

save.text: His right hand closes. The scar on his palm burns. Outside, the sunset flickers, as if the world had heard.

let_go.text: Saying it quietly hurts more than any wound of the last few nights. But for a second, the classroom clock moves. 21:47 becomes 21:48. Then it goes back.

unsure.text:
He doesn't decide. The clock stays stopped.

Maybe that's how all the other loops began. With an "I don't know".

loop_echo.text: Students will disappear today. He counts how many are left. Thirteen. Last loop there were fifteen. Something is speeding up.

core.text: Tenth day. Half the desks are empty. "Flu," says the teacher, reading a list of names that gets shorter as she reads it.

outro1.text: For the first time, all four are together in the same hallway, without planning it, without talking, just there.

outro1__2.text: Maya looks at the windows, Alice counts steps, Yuna holds Hikari's hand without noticing she's holding it, and Hikari lets her.

outro2.text: {player_name} stops a few steps away from them. He doesn't need to say anything. For the first time in a long while, the silence between the five of them isn't heavy. It's just a silence that fits.

start.text: The dawn looks painted. No clouds, no wind, every color a little too saturated. {player_name} opens the window and hears birds singing a melody that repeats every thirty seconds, identical.

intro2.text: On the street, the neighbors greet him with the same sentence: "Beautiful day, isn't it?" Yesterday he answered with a smile. Today he answers with a wave, and feels everyone noticed the difference.

too_perfect.text: No one is absent. No one remembers anything strange. The school looks freshly painted, without a scratch. Like a set built to convince someone to stay.

laugh.text:
In the hallway, a laugh. Loud. Carefree. Unmistakable.

{player_name} has known that laugh since he was six.

It's coming from the roof stairs.
choices: Stay in the courtyard, with the people who are still here.

follow.text:
At the foot of the stairs there's no one. Only the door, up above, closed.

And, written in the dust of the handrail with a finger, in handwriting that isn't his:

"you're coming tomorrow, right?"

stay.text:
He stays. He helps hang a lantern.

The laughter stops.

For some reason, that hurts more than if it had gone on.

loop_echo.text: He recognizes the beautiful day. The smell of bread. The same birdsong. This time he doesn't smile at the neighbors. They find it strange, and he likes that.

core.text: Eleventh day. Everything is perfect. Every desk occupied. The sun in the right place. The courtyard full of lanterns being set up for tomorrow, people laughing, music playing.

outro1.text: At the end of the day, once all the lanterns are hung, the principal goes through each classroom turning off the lights.

outro1__2.text: At the last one, he stops in the doorway, looks at {player_name} and whispers: "Everything will be in place tomorrow. I promise."

outro2.text: He says it like someone making a promise to himself. On his way out, the principal leaves the hallway light on. It's the only light in the school that stays on all night.

start.text: No one slept well. Breakfast went down tasteless, the books stayed unopened in the backpack.

start__2.text: At some point, between one cup and the next, {player_name} realized he'd written his own name on the bread wrapper, over and over, to make sure he was still himself.

intro2.text: The day passed slowly and quickly at once, the way the last days of anything do. In class, no one got any grades. The teachers just talked, and talked, and looked at the clock.

clock.text:
The courtyard clock reads 19:30.

At 21:47, it all ends. One way or another.

{player_name} has two hours.

girls.text: He sees the four of them in the crowd: Yuna on stage, holding the microphone with both hands. Alice checking her wristwatch every minute.

girls__2.text: Hikari near the stairs, arms crossed. And Maya, under the only unlit lantern, looking up at the roof.

choice.text: There's still time to talk to anyone he wants before going up.
choices: Take a deep breath and begin the night.

loop_echo.text: It's the night of the festival. Again. He thinks about how many times he has climbed these stairs, and realizes that, this time, he's thinking about how many times he came down.

core.text: Twelfth day. The night of the festival. The courtyard is lit by hundreds of paper lanterns. A fine rain begins to fall, like the first time.

outro1.text: As the sun goes down, the lanterns light themselves, one by one, from one end of the courtyard to the other. There's no one at the switch.

outro1__2.text: The students applaud as if it were part of the show. {player_name} is the only one not smiling.

outro2.text: Far away, high up, at the roof door, a white lantern sways in the wind. He watches it for a long time. When he blinks, it's already out.
